key_insight: Neuron ablation produces architecture-dependent language failures: gradual decline in LSTMs, threshold-like collapse under Transformer MLP ablation, and smoother sigmoid-like decline under attention-head ablation.
engineering_relevance: These distinct damage-response profiles can inform robustness testing of AI systems, though the study does not directly evaluate solid-mechanics applications.
method: Systematically ablate computational units in LSTM and Transformer language models.
Apply limited fine-tuning as a proxy for compensatory plasticity.
Compare language degradation under whole-unit, MLP, and attention-head ablation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports parallel syntactic and semantic decline in LSTMs, semantic substitutions and rising non-responses after MLP ablation, and reduced semantic specificity after attention-head ablation.
watch_item: Similarities to aphasia are qualitative; computational ablation and limited fine-tuning do not establish biological equivalence to neuronal loss and recovery.
paper_title: Can Language Models Get "Aphasia" From Neuronal Ablation?
